items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: So the first job that I played with my father when I was about 13 years old was a high school dance.

ctx.x: Okay, back then you have to realize that my house was a musician’s union, see? So scale in 1964, no in the late 50s in other words scale, basic scale was $12 for sidemen and then the leader was 5 dollars extra for the leader. And scale was minimum wage so to speak, if

you’re a union musician. Scale was $12 for the sideman and $5 extra for the leader. So the first job that I played with my father when I was about 13 years old was a high school dance. And I just, I played just clarinet at that time and so, by this time I’m going out to jam sessions with my brother-in-law and going to bars and things, to Sunday jam session. So my mother figured well since he’s hanging in these bars we might as well, you know, let him play with us. So my first job that I made, my father gave me…
